title: Hazel's Brilliant Best Window
markdown:
Sunlight blasted through Hazel the hedgehog's window, brilliant and rude in the nicest way.

"Today!" She popped up. Her quills tingled. Today was the Bramblebrook Brilliant Best Window competition. Every year the village transformed. Windows burst with color and clever crafts. This year, Hazel knew, was hers.

She dashed outside, a blur of brown spikes. Dewdrops sparkled. The grass was violently green. A cool breeze tickled her whiskers. Rafi the crow cawed from the old oak.

"Hazel! Ready to make some magic?"

"Rafi! My very best window yet." She bounced. Ideas whizzed. "But what says Hazel?"

Rafi tilted his head. "You have shiny pebbles. Fluffy dandelion seeds, like clouds. And you stack daisy chains."

Perfect. She gathered all morning. Pebbles from the brook, polished like minor jewels. Dandelion puffballs, light as air. Bright blue forget-me-nots, tiny sparks. She set them on the sill. It was not grand like Farmer Giles' pumpkins, nor intricate like Mrs. Higgins' quilt, nor towering like the baker's cakes. It was hers. Pure Hazel.

Then a mighty gust tumbled through Bramblebrook. Hazel yelped. The forget-me-nots scattered, tiny blue stars on the dusty path. The display looked ruined.

Rafi swooped, a black streak. "Hold on!" He gathered with quick pecks and tucked the flowers back. A few sat wobbly, a little out of line. Chaotic. Still there.

Soon came the clip-clop of Miss Birch's walking stick. Bramblebrook's judge. Everyone peeked. She smiled at Farmer Giles. "Such bounty." She admired Mrs. Higgins. "Such skill." Then she reached Hazel's cottage and stopped.

Kind eyes took in pebbles, puffballs, the slightly droopy re-tucked forget-me-nots.

"Oh, my. Pebbles for dreams of faraway lands?" She pointed to a grey stone. "Dandelion fluff for wishes?" She smiled at the cheerful mess. "And these flowers have had a grand adventure, just like you."

Hazel's heart thumped. She had not planned a story. She had planned a windowsill. Miss Birch was grafting meaning onto a gust, and somehow the graft took. The pebbles were from the bank where she imagined boats. The fluff did feel like wishes. The flowers had, in fact, traveled.

Miss Birch chuckled. "Bramblebrook has talented folk. The baker dreams of sky-high pastries. The librarian of stories that fly. Mr. Timson of boots that tap-dance." She looked at the sill. "You show us that small wishes, bravely held, and a little happy chaos, can be beautiful."

She tapped her chin. "The competition is for the best window. The most honest window is often the very best."

Clipboard up. "Hazel the hedgehog — this year's Brilliant Best Window!"

Cheers. Hazel gasped. Quills bristled with delight. Rafi cawed a jubilant song, which in crow was mostly more caw.

Miss Birch gave her a nod. "Don't let anyone tell you the little adventures aren't worth noticing."

Hazel beamed at her pebbles, her puffballs, her brave and slightly crooked flowers. The sun did the rest.

She whispered to Rafi, not to the day at large, "I wonder whether next year I should glue the forget-me-nots — or leave a gap, on purpose, in case the wind wants another scene."

Rafi, who had opinions about glue, hopped once on the sill as if to vote for chaos with a safety net.
